preText: 7:14pm We are all in readiness. Santhosh Kumar and Jagadeesan to open the batting. Warrier has the new ball for the Dragons - here we go! 7:07pm The last two matches at this venue have been won by the chasing side, meaning that Ashwin's decision to bowl first is not really a surprise. CSG, though, have the batting to put runs on the board and make scoreboard pressure a factor, especially with Jagadeesan and captain Aparajith slated to bat in the top three. Santhosh Kumar has not been in bad form either. Dindigul Dragons XI: Vimal Khumar, Shivam Singh, Baba Indrajith (wk), Boopathi Kumar, S Dinesh Raj, R Ashwin (capt), Varun Charavarthy, Suboth Bhati, VP Diran, P Vignesh, Sandeep Warrier DD bench: Sarath Kumar, K Aashiq, Om Nitin, G Kishoor Chepauk Super Gillies XI: D Santhosh Kumar, Narayan Jagadeesan (wk), Baba Aparajith (capt), Pradosh Ranjan Paul, Daryl Ferrario, C Andre Siddarth, Ganeshan Periyaswamy, Abhishek Tanwar, J Prem Kumar, Rahil Shah, M Silambarasan CSG bench: Balu Surya, Rajagopal Sathish, Mathan Kumar, B Iyappan 6:45pm Dindigul Dragons have won the toss and they have elected to field first. 6:15pm The Chepauk Super Gillies. The most decorated team in the Tamil Nadu Premier League. Five-time finalists, four-time winners. Led by Baba Aparajith, they'd most probably have had ambitions to win the entire thing again this year. But because of where they finished, they now have to take the longer and perhaps more arduous route, and have to win three on the trot to get to where they want to be. The Dindigul Dragons, while not as successful as CSG historically, have been in and around the latter stages before, having made the finals twice and having been a part of the playoffs as recently as last year. This has been a slightly inconsistent season so far, at least in terms of results, but they are back in the playoff mix, knowing that a three-game winning streak, like they produced earlier this season, will take them to their maiden TNPL title. So, here we are. In Dindigul, where the Dragons will likely be cheered on by a raucous and partisan home crowd. One of these sides, remember, will continue their campaign, clashing with Tiruppur Tamizhans on Friday to earn the right to play the defending champions in the final. One, though, will head back home, having seen their opportunity of a title snatched away from them. Hello and welcome to ESPNcricinfo's live coverage of the TNPL. It is the Eliminator, which as the name suggests, will eliminate one team. CSG have the title-winning pedigree of yore; the Dragons the hunger to end their TNPL hoodoo. This promises to be a classic, so without further ado, let's get stuck into the action!
